history.period: Current building established 2005; mythologically Satya Yuga / Mahabharata period
history.summary: A major Hindu temple in Arrah (Bhojpur district HQ), dedicated to Goddess Aranya Devi (Aranyani, goddess of the forest), regarded as the presiding deity of the city - the city of Arrah is named after her. The temple building is not old: it was established in 2005 at Sheesh Mahal Chowk on the north-east end of the city, and as of 2022 the old structure was being demolished and a new multi-storey building constructed (verify current status). Worship here is described as ancient: the Devi Bhagavata Purana recognises it as a Siddh Pitha among the 108 Shakti Pithas, and legends tie it to the Mahabharata period and to Rama, Lakshmana and Vishvamitra worshipping the goddess en route to Janakpur for the Dhanush Yagna. The sanctum houses twin black-stone idols (about 3 ft and 2 ft, said to be sisters), with marble statues of Ram, Sita and Krishna installed in 1953 by local merchants. CSV town/state (Arrah, Bihar) are correct.

name: Aranya Devi Temple
town_description: Arrah (officially Ara) is the headquarters of Bhojpur district in Bihar, a historic city on the Gangetic plain named after the goddess Aranya Devi of this temple. It is remembered for Veer Kunwar Singh's revolt against the British in 1857 and serves as a regional centre for agriculture, trade and pilgrimage.
